data.title: Fee demand (Gebührenbescheid) from "DSR Datenschutz-Registerstelle Europa UAB" – likely scam
data.summary: A company calling itself "DSR Datenschutz-Registerstelle Europa UAB" (Vilnius, Lithuania) claims a legal obligation to register personal-data processing and demands €498.00 ("Erfassungs-Nr. DSR-DE-26-447120"), payable by 29 July 2026 to a Lithuanian IBAN, threatening fines up to €20,000,000 and stating no objection is possible. This matches known GDPR-registration scam letters — there is no such statutory registration or fee requirement under the GDPR.
data.explanation: This letter has strong hallmarks of a scam: there is no legal requirement to "register" personal-data processing with any private company under the GDPR (Art. 30 DSGVO only requires companies to keep their own internal record, with no fee and no registry like this). Genuine German authorities do not demand payment to a foreign (Lithuanian) private account, do not threaten €20,000,000 fines for a missed private invoice, and always allow a legal remedy — here the letter explicitly denies that. Do not pay or reply with personal data. You can safely ignore it, but consider reporting it (e.g. to the Verbraucherzentrale or the police) and keep it as evidence if contacted again.

items.action: Do not pay without first verifying this claim; it shows strong signs of being a scam rather than a real legal obligation.
items.consequence: The sender claims it will report the matter to a data-protection authority and threatens fines up to €20,000,000, but this threat is not credible for a private invoice.
items.quote: Zahlen Sie die Gebühr bis zum 29.07.2026 auf das Konto IBAN LT21 7044 0000 0447 1229

warnings: This strongly resembles a known scam pattern (fake "Datenschutz-Registerstelle"/GDPR registration demand): there is no statutory fee or registry of this kind under the GDPR.
The payment account is a Lithuanian IBAN for what is framed as a German/EU legal obligation, which is a common red flag for fraudulent invoices.
The letter denies any right to object ("Ein Widerspruch gegen die Erfassung ist nicht möglich") and restricts contact to e-mail only, both typical pressure tactics used in scam letters.
The threatened fine of up to €20,000,000 for non-payment of a private invoice is not a credible legal consequence.
